items.summary: “My parents called me worried when this incident happened. I just moved to Delhi for college and this situation has scared me. I hope we are safe,” a first-year student from Shri Venkateshwara College told Newslaundry , requesting anonymity. A resident of Bihar, she lives in one of the many paying guest accommodations in Satya Niketan, a locality popular with Delhi University students. On Sunday afternoon, a five-storey PG known as Hostel Daze collapsed, trapping several people inside and triggering a frantic rescue operation. Construction or repair work was underway on the ground floor of the building when it collapsed, according to eyewitnesses. Chaos and panic unfolded in the area as students, residents, police and rescue personnel rushed to the site. Apart from PG residents, construction workers are also feared to be trapped in rubble. At the time of writing this report, 10 had been pulled out, of whom five are dead, according to the police. Those rescued were taken to the AIIMS Trauma Centre, where they were stated to be in critical condition, officials said. The exact number of those still trapped remained unclear. Several news reports put the number at around 20 to 25, while residents in Satya Niketan claimed that at least 40 people may have been affected. Since the collapse took place on a Sunday, when many students would have been inside their rooms, residents feared the toll could rise. Multiple Delhi Fire Services and NDRF teams, including search and rescue and breathing apparatus units, were deployed, along with water bowser units. Residents, including students, also rushed to the spot and helped with the initial rescue effort. items.title: Former Supreme Court Justice Krishna Murari joins Vantara's Governing Council
items.summary: Former Supreme Court Justice Krishna Murari has been appointed as a member of Vantrara's independent governing council to oversee conservation, rescue and compliance work. Vantara is a Reliance Industries-backed animal rescue centre in Gujarat's Jamnagar. Former Secretary General of the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES), John E Scanlon AO was appointed as Chair of the council in August this year. Justice Murari studied law from Allahabad University and enrolled as an advocate on December 23, 1981. He began his practice at the Allahabad High Court, where he was appointed as an additional judge on January 7, 2004. He became a permanent judge in 2005, and in June 2018, he was elevated as Chief Justice of the Punjab and Haryana High Court. He was elevated as a judge of the Supreme Court on September 23, 2019. He retired from the Supreme Court in July 2023.

However, the State government has alleged that the decision was taken without its consent. Justice Mishra is set to be administered the oath of office at Punjab Lok Bhavan in Chandigarh on Monday. Hours before the ceremony, the Punjab cabinet convened an emergency meeting via video conference to protest the Centre’s decision to appoint Justice Mishra as Chief Justice. In a resolution passed following the meeting, the government urged the Governor not to administer the oath to Justice Mishra until the government gives its consent for the same. "Taking serious exception to the appointment of Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra as Chief Justice of the Punjab and Haryana High Court without awaiting the views of the Punjab Government, the Cabinet resolved that the appointment and administration of oath should be put on hold until Punjab’s views are obtained and duly considered," the government said in a statement. The government said that under the ‘Memorandum of Procedure for Appointment and Transfer of Chief Justices and Judges of High Court’, the Union Minister of Law, Justice and Company Affairs is required to obtain the views of the concerned State government after receipt of a recommendation from the Chief Justice of India. items.title: Delhi court sends Swatantra Bhardwaj to judicial custody for a day in Jantar Mantar assault case
items.summary: A Delhi court on Sunday sent right-wing influencer Swatantra Bhardwaj to judicial custody (JC) for a day in the case related to alleged assault on the father of a Dalit student-activist during the Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) protests at Jantar Mantar in July. Duty Magistrate Anjali Singh of the Patiala House Court passed the order. According to a lawyer involved in the case, Bhardwaj was produced at the judge's residence through virtual conference (VC). Police asked him to be sent to JC for 14 days. However, since he was produced before the Duty Magistrate, Bhardwaj was sent to JC for a day. The request for additional custody will be decided by the concerned court on Monday. Bhardwaj was arrested from Uttar Pradesh yesterday. He has been booked for offence of assault and provisions under the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act [SC/ST Act] and the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (POCSO Act). Bhardwaj was initially booked only for the offences under Sections 115(2) (causing simple hurt) and 126(2) (wrongful restraint) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). He later took to social media and claimed that had cracked the skull of the girl's father and was detained by the police only for a few hours. He also claimed proximity to NDA leaders Kapil Mishra and Chirag Paswan. Paswan denied the same and also lodged a separate complaint against Bhardwaj for misusing his name. Meanwhile, after Cockroach Janta Party leaders along with the girl and her father protested at the Parliament Street police station, more serious charges were added and he was arrested.

items.title: Centre clears appointment of Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi as Chief Justice of Bombay High Court
items.summary: The Central government on Saturday cleared the appointment of Allahabad High Court Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi as the new Chief Justice of the Bombay High Court. Justice Tripathi will be the 50th Chief Justice of the High Court and the second Chief Justice from Allahabad High Court. The recommendation for his appointment as the Chief Justice was made by the Supreme Court Collegium at a meeting held on August 6. Justice Tripathi graduated in law from Lucknow University in 1990. He enrolled as an advocate on January 11, 1992. His practice was mainly on the civil side. He served as the additional chief standing counsel for the State of Uttar Pradesh since October 2007. He also appeared as counsel for the Kanpur Development Authority, Kanpur Nagar Nigam, UP Food and Essential Commodities Corporation, Agra Development Authority, Moradabad Development Authority and Kumaun University. Justice Tripathi was elevated as an additional judge of the Allahabad High Court on September 27, 2013. He was made a permanent judge on April 10, 2015. items.title: Centre clears appointment of Justice Sanjay Kumar Agrawal as Chief Justice of Rajasthan High Court
items.summary: The Central government on Saturday cleared the appointment of Justice Sanjay Kumar Agrawal as the Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court. The appointment comes pursuant to a recommendation made by the Supreme Court Collegium on August 31. Justice Agrawal is currently the Acting Chief Justice of the Chhattisgarh High Court. He was elevated as an additional judge of that Court in September 2013 and made a permanent judge in March 2016. His elevation as Chief Justice comes amid a controversy over the conduct of the present Acting Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court, Justice Sanjeev Prakash Sharma . Supreme Court Justice Sandeep Mehta had recently written to Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant seeking Justice Sharma's transfer out of Rajasthan and appointment of a regular Chief Justice from another High Court. Justice Mehta had raised allegations concerning Justice Sharma's exercise of administrative powers and the listing of cases. The controversy also triggered protests by lawyers at both the Jaipur and Jodhpur benches of the Rajasthan High Court, with lawyers demanding that Justice Sharma be divested of his charge as Acting Chief Justice. Justice Sharma, who is set to retire later this month, has denied the allegations against him. [Read notification]
